andeancat: A scientific field-guide illustration of an Andean cat standing on all four feet in STRICT SIDE PROFILE. A small stocky high-mountain cat with long thick soft ash-grey fur marked with rusty brown and dark grey blotches and vertical bar-like stripes down its flanks and shoulders. ITS MUZZLE IS CLEAN AND EVENLY PALE: the short fur from below the eyes forward over the bridge of the nose, the whisker pads and the chin is one uniform creamy white-grey, unmarked and unshaded, ending at a small black nose. The only dark marks on the head are two narrow rust-brown bars on each cheek, set well back beside the ear and clear of the muzzle. Large rounded ears, and a very thick bushy tail ringed with six to nine broad dark bands and a pale tip.
greaterhorseshoebat: A scientific field-guide illustration of a greater horseshoe bat in flight, both wings spread wide to either side, seen from the front. ITS NOSE CARRIES A SMALL FLESHY PALE PINK-GREY STRUCTURE THAT COVERS ONLY THE NOSE ITSELF, no wider than the gap between its eyes and no taller than one eye: a low rounded horseshoe-shaped flap wrapped around both nostrils, a small upright ridge at its centre, and a short blunt point above it. The rest of the face is ordinary soft grey-brown fur, and the cheeks, forehead and chin are furred and bare of any flap. THE WINGS ARE BROAD AND END IN WIDE BLUNT ROUNDED TIPS, each wingtip curving smoothly round in a wide arc and as broad across as the middle of the wing. Very large broad pointed ears, small dark eyes almost buried in fur, greyish-brown wing membranes.
freetailbat: A scientific field-guide illustration of a Mexican free-tailed bat in flight, both wings spread wide to either side, seen from the front. Long narrow pointed wings of dark grey-brown leather built for speed. ITS TAIL IS SHORT: a slim bare tapering tip projects past the rear edge of the tail membrane by ABOUT THE LENGTH OF ONE OF ITS OWN TOES AND NO MORE, a small blunt stub barely clear of the membrane, thin and unremarkable. The membrane between its ankles is broad and the tail scarcely passes it. Broad forward-tilted ears that nearly meet over its forehead, a wrinkled upper lip, bristly toes, dark grey-brown fur.
dugong: A scientific field-guide illustration of a dugong in STRICT SIDE PROFILE, swimming level. A smooth heavy grey body tapering to a broad whale-like fluked tail. THE FRONT OF THE HEAD IS THE POINT: the muzzle is a LARGE SQUARED-OFF FLESHY BLOCK that turns sharply DOWNWARD so its whole flat front face points at the sea floor, and the MOUTH OPENS ON THE UNDERSIDE OF THAT BLOCK, not at the tip and not at the front. The downturned face is a broad flat bristled pad, wider than it is tall, covered in short stiff whiskers, with two small crescent nostrils set high on top of the snout near its upper edge. A small dark eye sits far back on the side of the head. Short paddle-like flippers low on the chest.
fiddlercrab: A scientific field-guide illustration of a male fiddler crab on sand, seen from above and slightly in front. A small square-bodied crab with ONE VASTLY OVERSIZED BRIGHTLY COLOURED CLAW nearly as large as its whole body held up before it, and the other claw tiny by comparison. IT HAS EXACTLY TWO EYES AND ONE MOUTH: the two eyes sit side by side at the centre of the front edge of the shell, each a small dark bead on top of a slender upright stalk, the two stalks close together and the same length; below them is a SINGLE SMALL MOUTH, one neat opening at the centre of the face. Nowhere else on the animal is there an eye or a mouth. Eight slender walking legs, four on each side.
fishingbat: A scientific field-guide illustration of a greater bulldog bat, also called the fishing bat, in STRICT SIDE PROFILE flying low with its body level and its head to the left. Bright rusty-orange fur and long narrow pointed wings of orange-brown leather. ITS HIND LEGS AND FEET ARE THE POINT: the legs reach down and forward below the body, and the feet are ENORMOUS, each foot as long as the bat's own head, armed with long curved hooked claws held open. Its head is small, furry and wedge-shaped with a neat pointed muzzle, full cheeks, a divided upper lip and two tall upright pointed ears. Small dark eyes.
hectorsdolphin: A scientific field-guide illustration of a Hector's dolphin in STRICT SIDE PROFILE, swimming level. A small stocky dolphin with a low rounded forehead and no beak. ITS MARKINGS ARE THE POINT AND THEY ARE CRISP-EDGED, NOT BLURRED: the back and sides are PALE SILVER-GREY; a solid BLACK MASK covers the whole face from the tip of the snout back through the eye and down to the throat; the flippers and the dorsal fin are SOLID BLACK; a broad BLACK BAND runs along the tail stock. The throat, chest and belly are CLEAN WHITE, and a narrow white finger reaches up onto the flank behind each flipper. ITS DORSAL FIN IS A LOW BLACK SEMICIRCLE, the trailing edge curving smoothly round with no point and no backward hook, standing no taller than half the depth of the body.
horseshoecrab: A scientific field-guide illustration of a horseshoe crab seen in STRICT SIDE PROFILE from ground level, the animal standing on sand with its head to the left. From this angle the domed brown carapace reads as a LOW SMOOTH ARCH rising from the sand in one even curve, thickest at the front and sloping down to the rear. Behind it the smaller hinged rear section is edged with short spines, and from that a long rigid pointed spike tail trails straight out behind, held slightly above the sand. The pale jointed legs are just visible beneath the rim of the shell. Two small dark compound eyes sit on the upper slope of the arch, one on each side.
irrawaddy: A scientific field-guide illustration of an Irrawaddy dolphin in STRICT SIDE PROFILE, swimming level. ITS PROPORTIONS ARE THE POINT: the body is LONG AND SLENDER, running from the front of the head to the tail flukes at ABOUT SIX TIMES ITS OWN GREATEST DEPTH, a smooth even tube that tapers gently to the tail. THE HEAD IS A SMOOTH ROUNDED DOME with no beak at all: seen from the side the forehead rises in one continuous curve from the mouthline over the top of the head, the front of the face is blunt and evenly rounded with no flat or angle anywhere on it, and a shallow neck crease marks where the head meets the body. A rounded mouthline gives a faint upward curve. Pale bluish-grey. A very small low rounded dorsal fin sits well back along the body and barely rises from the back.
lavalizard: A scientific field-guide illustration of a lava lizard standing on volcanic rock in STRICT SIDE PROFILE. A slim lizard with a dark grey-black scaled back finely speckled with pale gold, a long tapering tail and slender clawed feet. ITS THROAT IS BRIGHT RED: the whole underside of the head from the chin back to the base of the neck is a vivid scarlet patch, clearly bounded and unmistakable against the dark body. The belly behind it is pale grey.
leafyseadragon: A scientific field-guide illustration of a leafy sea dragon HELD HORIZONTAL AND LEVEL, its long axis lying flat across the picture from left to right, head at the left and tail stretched straight out behind it at the right, drifting on its side the way a pipefish swims. Its body is smothered in an elaborate profusion of long ornate leaf-shaped skin appendages sprouting in every direction from its head, neck, back, belly and tail, broad flat golden-green fronds so numerous that the outline of the animal is almost lost inside them. A long thin tubular snout points forward and level. The body is straight and horizontal from end to end and the tail does not curl.
sealamprey: A scientific field-guide illustration of a sea lamprey with its head turned to face the viewer and its mouth held wide open, filling the front of the picture. THE MOUTH IS THE POINT: a large perfectly ROUND FUNNEL with no jaws, its inner surface covered in MANY CONCENTRIC RINGS OF SHARP CURVED YELLOW HORNY TEETH growing smaller ring by ring toward the dark throat at the centre, and a thick rasping toothed tongue rising in the middle of them. The rim of the disc is a thick fleshy lip. Behind the head a slender mottled grey-brown eel-like body trails away, with one small round eye and a row of SEVEN small round gill holes behind it in a straight line.
seaotter: A scientific field-guide illustration of a sea otter floating ON ITS BACK at the surface, body horizontal and belly upward, head to the left and raised just clear of the water. Dense dark brown fur, a broad pale grizzled face with a blunt muzzle and long white whiskers, small round ears. IT HOLDS ONE SEA URCHIN AGAINST ITS CHEST IN BOTH FOREPAWS: a single round purple urchin covered in short blunt spines, no wider than the otter's own head, gripped between two small dark paws. Its hind feet are broad flattened webbed flippers held at the surface.
seasquirt: A scientific field-guide illustration of a COLONY OF SEA SQUIRTS on a rock, seen from the side. SEVERAL SEPARATE INDIVIDUALS, six or seven of them, stand side by side on the same grey rock, each one its own soft translucent rubbery orange-pink tube rooted to the stone at its base and rising a short way from it. They are of slightly different heights and lean at slightly different angles, and there are visible gaps of bare rock between them. EACH INDIVIDUAL CARRIES TWO SHORT OPEN SIPHON TUBES AT ITS TOP. Simple sac-shaped animals with no arms, no legs and no face.
eagleray: A scientific field-guide illustration of a spotted eagle ray SEEN FROM DIRECTLY ABOVE, gliding level and flat. ITS OUTLINE IS ONE SMOOTH FLATTENED DIAMOND, the same clean uninterrupted profile as a stingray: the body and the wings form a single continuous disc with no step and no notch where they meet, the leading edges sweeping out in a shallow unbroken curve from the head to the wide pointed wingtips and the trailing edges sweeping back to meet the tail. The disc is markedly WIDER FROM TIP TO TIP THAN IT IS LONG. At the front the head projects a little as a rounded flattened duck-bill snout. A very long thin whip-like tail trails straight out behind, several times the length of the disc. Deep blue-black above, covered in dense evenly spaced white rings and spots.
sunflowerstar: A scientific field-guide illustration of a sunflower sea star SEEN FROM DIRECTLY ABOVE, resting flat on rock. IT HAS MANY ARMS: TWENTY-FOUR SLENDER ARMS radiate evenly all the way round a wide soft central disc, spaced close together so their bases touch and form a continuous ring, each arm about twice as long as the disc is wide and tapering to a fine tip. The arms lie flat and spread evenly in every direction with no gap wider than one arm anywhere around the circle. Soft mottled purple and orange skin covered in fine short blunt spines, and rows of pale tube feet along the underside of each arm.
weedyseadragon: A scientific field-guide illustration of a weedy seadragon held HORIZONTAL with its tail stretched straight out behind it, drifting level. ITS BODY IS SMOOTH: the trunk and tail are clean rounded surfaces crossed by low soft bony bands that barely raise the outline, and the profile from snout to tail tip runs in one gentle unbroken line. A FEW SMALL LEAF-SHAPED FLAPS OF SKIN, about eight in all, hang from its back and belly, each one soft, rounded and no longer than the depth of its own body, spaced well apart. A long straight tubular snout, a slender body, reddish-orange skin crossed by purple-blue bands and dotted with bright yellow spots. The tail is straight and tapering and does not curl.
oryx: A scientific field-guide illustration of an Arabian oryx standing on all four legs in STRICT SIDE PROFILE. A compact white antelope with a pure chalk-white body and long straight ringed horns rising from the top of its head. ITS MARKINGS ARE ALMOST BLACK: a deep blackish-brown mask covers the front of the face from between the horns down the length of the nose, a second dark band runs from the eye down the cheek, the throat carries a dark patch, and each leg is banded with the SAME NEAR-BLACK COLOUR from the knee and hock down to the hoof. The tail is tipped with the same dark shade. Every marking is a strong dark brown so deep it reads as black against the white coat.
bilby: A scientific field-guide illustration of a greater bilby standing on all four feet in STRICT SIDE PROFILE. ITS LEGS ARE SHORT: each leg is only about ONE THIRD THE DEPTH OF ITS OWN BODY, so the animal stands low with its belly close to the ground and its back running almost level. Soft blue-grey fur, very large upright thin-skinned ears, a long pointed pink snout, and a long tail that is grey at the base and boldly white along its outer half.
emu: A scientific field-guide illustration of an emu standing in STRICT SIDE PROFILE. ITS BODY IS A BROAD HORIZONTAL OVAL: the trunk is clearly LONGER FROM CHEST TO RUMP THAN IT IS DEEP FROM BACK TO BELLY, carried level and slung low between the legs, deepest at the middle and rounded at both ends. From the front of that oval a long slim neck rises steeply to a small head. Shaggy drooping grey-brown plumage hangs from the body and hides the wings. Long powerful bare grey legs with three toes.
jerboa: A scientific field-guide illustration of a long-eared jerboa STANDING ON BOTH HIND FEET, seen in STRICT SIDE PROFILE, its body upright and its weight on two very long thin hind legs. THE HIND LEGS ARE THE POINT: each hind foot and shin together are AS LONG AS THE WHOLE BODY FROM SHOULDER TO RUMP, bare, slender and stilt-like, with the animal balanced high on them. Its forelimbs are TINY, no longer than one of its own ears, held tucked against its chest. A LONG THIN NAKED TAIL, twice the length of the body, trails behind and ends in a flat black-and-white tuft. Sandy tan fur, enormous thin upright ears, a short blunt muzzle and large black eyes.
longnosedbat: A scientific field-guide illustration of a lesser long-nosed bat in flight, hovering with both wings spread wide to either side, seen from the front. ITS MUZZLE IS SHORT AND ORDINARY: the snout projects only a little way in front of its eyes, ABOUT AS LONG AS ONE OF ITS OWN EYES IS WIDE, a neat blunt cone that ends in a small dark nose with a tiny triangular flap of skin at the tip. The face is compact and rounded, with the eyes set well forward and the muzzle no more than a small projection beyond them. A narrow pink tongue extends a short way from the tip. Cinnamon-brown fur dusted with pale yellow pollen around the face and shoulders, narrow pointed wings, small ears, dark eyes.
rattlesnake: A scientific field-guide illustration of a rattlesnake coiled with its head raised and its tail lifted clear of the coils. AT THE VERY TIP OF THE TAIL, GROWING STRAIGHT OUT OF IT AND TOUCHING IT, is a SMALL RATTLE: a short stack of five or six dry interlocking horny segments forming one tapering column NO THICKER THAN THE TAIL ITSELF AT THE POINT WHERE IT JOINS, and no longer than the width of the snake's own head. It is a modest tip to the tail, not a large object. A thick muscular tan body with dark brown diamond blotches edged in cream, a broad triangular head, vertical pupils, heat pits.
beagle: A scientific field-guide illustration of a Beagle standing on all four legs in STRICT SIDE PROFILE. IT HAS ONE TAIL ONLY: a single short tail at the rump, carried UP and slightly forward, tipped with white, and there is nothing hanging beneath or behind the dog. ITS TRICOLOUR COAT IS IN CLEAN SOLID BLOCKS WITH SMOOTH EDGES: one continuous BLACK SADDLE covers the back and upper flanks as a single unbroken patch with a smooth curved border, the head, ears and legs are even warm TAN, and the muzzle, throat, chest, feet and tail tip are clean WHITE. The three colours meet along tidy edges. Long floppy ears, a square muzzle and a black nose.
bordercollie: A scientific field-guide illustration of a border collie standing on all four legs in STRICT SIDE PROFILE. A medium herding dog in black and white: SOLID UNBROKEN BLACK covers the whole back, both flanks, the hindquarters and the outside of every leg down to the wrist, running without interruption from the shoulder to the tail and DOWN PAST THE BELLY LINE ON THE SIDE FACING THE VIEWER, so the flank between the front and hind legs is entirely black. The white is confined to a blaze up the muzzle and forehead, a broad collar around the neck, the chest between the front legs, the four feet and the tail tip. Bushy tail, alert ears.
earthworm: A scientific field-guide illustration of a common earthworm lying on dark soil, its body curved in a loose S. ITS BODY IS A SMOOTH UNBROKEN CYLINDER FROM END TO END, pinkish-brown, ringed with many fine close-set segment grooves, tapering to a point at the head and flattening slightly at the tail. THE OUTLINE IS PERFECTLY CLEAN ALONG BOTH SIDES: nothing projects from it anywhere, no limbs, no legs, no feet, no bristles, no antennae, no appendages of any kind, only bare smooth skin. A slightly swollen smooth pale band circles the body about a third of the way along.
bordeauxmastiff: A scientific field-guide illustration of a Dogue de Bordeaux SEEN IN STRICT SIDE PROFILE, standing squarely on all four legs with its body turned fully broadside to the viewer and its head in true profile facing left, so the whole length of the dog from chest to rump lies flat across the picture. A massive muscular body on short heavy legs, deep broad chest, short reddish-fawn coat. Seen from the side the head is very large and blocky with a short deeply upturned muzzle, heavy hanging jowls, and deep folds of loose skin across the brow and down the cheek. Small dark eyes and small folded ears set high.
duck: A scientific field-guide illustration of a domestic white duck standing in STRICT SIDE PROFILE. A plump white farmyard duck with a broad flat orange bill, orange webbed feet, a rounded body and a short upcurled tail. ITS WHOLE UNDERSIDE IS EVENLY PALE: the breast, belly and the underside of the body are the SAME CLEAN CREAMY WHITE AS THE BACK, shaded only by a soft even light grey that deepens smoothly and gradually toward the lowest edge of the belly, with no dark patches, no mottling and no sharp-edged shadow anywhere. The plumage reads as one continuous white surface from head to tail.
koi: A scientific field-guide illustration of a koi in STRICT SIDE PROFILE, swimming level with its head to the left. ITS BODY IS LONG: from the snout to the base of the tail it measures ABOUT FOUR TIMES ITS OWN GREATEST DEPTH, a slim elongated torpedo that tapers evenly toward the tail rather than a short deep oval. A large ornamental carp, white patterned with vivid orange and black patches, with a long low dorsal fin running much of the length of the back, paired barbels at the corners of the mouth, and a broad forked tail.
tabbycat: A scientific field-guide illustration of a tabby cat sitting upright in three-quarter view. AN ORDINARY DOMESTIC HOUSE CAT with a plain short coat. ITS COLOUR IS COOL GREY: the ground colour is a soft silvery blue-grey over the whole body, marked with darker charcoal-grey swirling stripes along the flanks, rings on the legs and tail, and an M-shaped mark on the forehead. Every colour in the coat is grey or charcoal. A rounded head with medium upright ears, round amber eyes, white chin and chest, and a long tail. An ordinary domestic pet cat with a plain grey coat.
lyrebird: A scientific field-guide illustration of a superb lyrebird standing on forest ground in STRICT SIDE PROFILE, its long tail carried BEHIND IT AND TRAILING DOWN CLOSE TO THE GROUND rather than raised or spread. The bird itself is a large plain sooty-brown ground bird with strong grey legs, a slender pointed dark bill, a rounded body and a long neck. ITS TAIL IS A NARROW TRAILING BUNDLE OF SEPARATE FEATHERS lying close together, not a broad sheet: two long outer feathers curve gently outward at the very end, and between them hang about twelve fine SILVER-WHITE FILAMENTARY PLUMES, each one thin, wispy and separate, hanging in a slender close-gathered train. The tail is entirely brown, grey and silver-white, and every feather is a separate narrow strand.
tasdevil: A scientific field-guide illustration of a Tasmanian devil standing on four legs in STRICT SIDE PROFILE, drawn realistically with sober naturalistic shading. ITS BUILD IS SHORT AND COMPACT: the body from chest to rump is only ABOUT TWICE THE DEPTH OF ITS OWN CHEST, a squat barrel-shaped marsupial standing LOW on very short thick legs, with a broad heavy head almost as wide as its shoulders and no visible neck. The back is short and slightly arched and the belly sits close to the ground. Coarse black fur, a broad white band across the chest and a second white patch on the rump. Its mouth is firmly closed, lips together, expression calm. A thick blunt muzzle with a pink nose, small round pink-rimmed ears, small dark eyes, and a short thick tapering tail no longer than half the body.
asiangoldencat: A scientific field-guide illustration of an Asian golden cat standing on all four legs in STRICT SIDE PROFILE. A medium solidly built cat with a plain unmarked uniform foxy golden-red coat over the whole body. ITS MUZZLE IS EVENLY PALE AND UNMARKED: the whisker pads, the bridge of the nose and the chin are one clean creamy white, smooth and uniform from the eyes forward to a small pink-brown nose. The facial markings are confined to the upper face, well above the muzzle: a bold white stripe edged in black runs from the inner corner of each eye up over the crown, and a white streak crosses each cheek beside the ear. Small rounded ears dark on the back, and a long tail whose last third is white underneath.
bandicoot: A scientific field-guide illustration of an eastern barred bandicoot standing on all four feet in STRICT SIDE PROFILE. A small marsupial with greyish-brown fur, a long pointed pink snout, large thin upright ears and a short thin tail. THE BARS ARE THE POINT AND THEY ARE BOLD: THREE OR FOUR BROAD PALE CREAM STRIPES run ACROSS the hindquarters from the spine down the flank, set at right angles to the backbone, evenly spaced, each as wide as the animal's own eye and standing out clearly against the darker fur around them. They cover the rump and the rear flank only, and the shoulders and neck in front of them are plain.
skink: A scientific field-guide illustration of a blue-tongued skink lying flat on all four legs with its belly touching the ground, seen in STRICT SIDE PROFILE, its mouth open and its tongue extended. ITS SKIN IS BROWN AND GREY ONLY: a broad flat head and a low heavy body scaled in warm silvery grey-brown and crossed by darker chocolate bands, with a cream underside and a tapering banded tail, and every scale on the head, body, legs and tail is brown, grey or cream. THE ONLY BLUE ON THE ENTIRE ANIMAL IS ITS TONGUE, a broad flat bright cobalt-blue tongue held out from the open mouth. Very short stubby legs, small dark eyes.
capuchin: A scientific field-guide illustration of a tufted capuchin on all fours on a branch, seen in STRICT SIDE PROFILE with its head turned slightly toward the viewer. ITS FACE IS A MONKEY'S FACE: the muzzle projects forward well beyond the eyes as a short blunt cone, the nostrils open sideways at its tip, the jaw is deep and the chin slopes back and away with no point, the brow is a low straight ridge of fur, and the whole face is small and rounded with the eyes set close together and low. Black and buff fur, a cap of dark fur with two small tufts on the crown, dark cheeks, and a thick prehensile tail curling behind.
bobcat: A scientific field-guide illustration of a bobcat standing on all four legs in STRICT SIDE PROFILE. ITS TAIL IS A SHORT STUB HELD UP: a thick stumpy tail only ABOUT AS LONG AS THE CAT'S OWN EAR, carried ERECT AND POINTING UPWARD clear of the hindquarters, black across the upper surface and white underneath, ending bluntly. A medium tawny-brown wildcat spotted with dark markings, a broad face framed by a flared cheek ruff of long fur, upright ears with short black tufts and white spots on their black backs, long legs and large paws.
chameleon: A scientific field-guide illustration of a veiled chameleon gripping a horizontal branch, seen in STRICT SIDE PROFILE. THE BODY IS HELD HORIZONTAL ALONG THE BRANCH, back level and belly close to the wood, with ALL FOUR FEET CLAMPED ROUND THE BRANCH, each foot split into two opposed bundles of toes that pinch the wood from above and below. The four legs are bent and splayed out to the sides beneath the body, carrying its weight from either side, and the tail is coiled in a tight spiral beneath the branch. A tall casque rises from the back of the head, the flanks are flattened and deep and banded in vivid green and yellow, and the eyes are independently swivelling turrets.
monarch_p: A scientific field-guide illustration of a monarch chrysalis hanging beneath a leafy twig. THE CHRYSALIS IS A SINGLE SMOOTH SEALED CASE: a plain rounded jade-green pod with an unbroken glossy surface and a delicate line of gold dots near its top, tapering to a small black stalk at the very top by which it hangs. NOTHING GROWS OUT OF THE CHRYSALIS ANYWHERE: no leaf, no stem, no shoot and no green blade emerges from its surface or its base, and its outline is a clean uninterrupted curve all the way round. ABOVE IT AND SEPARATE FROM IT is a brown woody twig bearing several ordinary green leaves, and the chrysalis hangs clear below the twig on its short stalk with visible space between the case and the nearest leaf.
civet: A scientific field-guide illustration of an African civet standing on all four legs in STRICT SIDE PROFILE. ITS BUILD IS SLENDER: the trunk is a NARROW SHALLOW TUBE no deeper from back to belly than the width of its own head, long and low and slim, with a clear gap of daylight beneath the belly between the front and hind legs and a visible waist in front of the hips. A long pointed snout, coarse grey fur covered in rows of black spots and blotches, a black facial mask, a crest of longer hair along the spine, and a thick bushy ringed tail.
colobus: A scientific field-guide illustration of a black-and-white colobus SITTING UPRIGHT ON A BRANCH, seen in STRICT SIDE PROFILE. It sits on its haunches with its BACK VERTICAL AND ITS CHEST FACING FORWARD, its two hind feet gripping the branch beneath it and its two hands resting on its knees, its head level and looking ahead. It is a monkey seated in a tree, at rest and alert, with none of its weight on its hands. Glossy black fur with a long sweeping white mantle of hair hanging from its shoulders down both flanks, a white frame of hair around a bare dark face, and a very long white-tufted tail hanging straight down below the branch.
dormouse: A scientific field-guide illustration of a hazel dormouse sitting on a branch holding a hazelnut in both forepaws, seen in STRICT SIDE PROFILE. ITS TAIL IS SLIM: a narrow tapering tail about as long as its body, covered in SHORT FLAT CLOSE-LYING FUR THE SAME LENGTH AS THE FUR ON ITS BACK, so the tail stays a thin even rod from base to tip with a smooth outline and only a slight thickening at the very end. Golden-orange fur, large round black eyes, small rounded ears and a blunt muzzle with long whiskers.
echidna: A scientific field-guide illustration of a short-beaked echidna standing on forest ground in STRICT SIDE PROFILE. A round domed body carried low on short legs. ITS COLOURING IS BROWN THROUGHOUT: the dense coarse fur between the spines is DARK CHOCOLATE BROWN, and the spines themselves are WARM TAN-BROWN at the base deepening to dark brown at their tips, so the whole animal reads as a rich brown mound. A long thin bare dark snout projects straight forward from the front of the body, and stout dark clawed feet show below.
firesalamander: A scientific field-guide illustration of a fire salamander standing on damp ground in STRICT SIDE PROFILE. A glossy black body with bold irregular yellow-orange blotches, four short splayed legs and a rounded tail. ITS EYES STAND PROUD OF ITS HEAD: each eye is a large glossy black dome that BULGES UPWARD AND OUTWARD ABOVE THE LINE OF THE SKULL, rising clearly above the flat top of the head so its curve breaks the profile. Behind and below each eye the head is smooth glossy skin running unbroken to the jaw, with a low swollen gland on the side of the head; THE SIDE OF THE HEAD IS COMPLETELY SMOOTH, with no ear, no ear flap, no ear opening and nothing projecting from it. A wide straight mouthline and small nostrils at the blunt snout.
flyingsquirrel: A scientific field-guide illustration of a flying squirrel gliding, seen from directly above with all four limbs stretched straight out sideways. THE MEMBRANE IS LARGE: a broad flap of furry skin runs from each wrist to each ankle and is stretched WIDE AND TAUT, so that the animal's outline is a BROAD RECTANGLE ALMOST AS WIDE ACROSS AS IT IS LONG, the skin filling the whole space between front and hind legs on each side and bulging slightly outward past the limbs. It is loose body skin continuous with the flanks and covered in the same soft grey-brown fur as the back, with a fine dark edge along its rim. Soft grey-brown fur, a cream belly, enormous round black eyes, and a broad flat bushy tail held straight out behind.
giantmillipede: A scientific field-guide illustration of a giant African millipede STRETCHED OUT STRAIGHT along the ground, seen in STRICT SIDE PROFILE, its whole length lying flat from left to right in one long gentle curve. IT IS NOT COILED and its body does not cross itself. AT THE LEFT END IS A CLEARLY VISIBLE HEAD, slightly broader and more rounded than the segments behind it, carrying TWO SHORT SEGMENTED ANTENNAE pointing forward, a pair of small dark eye patches and a blunt mouth beneath. Behind the head the long thick glossy black-brown body runs away in many identical rings, each ring bearing two pairs of short pale legs, and the whole underside is a dense even fringe of legs.
howler: A scientific field-guide illustration of a black howler monkey on all fours on a branch, both hands and both feet flat on the wood, seen in STRICT SIDE PROFILE. ITS FUR IS BLACK: long shaggy hair of a deep uniform coal-black over the head, back, flanks, limbs and tail, with no red, no orange and no brown anywhere in the coat. A barrel-shaped torso with a back sloping from high shoulders, the head carried low and forward, a deep bearded jaw and a swollen throat, a bare dark face, and a thick prehensile tail curling behind. It stands on four legs as an animal.
mara: A scientific field-guide illustration of a Patagonian mara standing on all four legs in STRICT SIDE PROFILE. ITS LEGS ARE SHORT: each leg from body to ground is only ABOUT HALF THE DEPTH OF ITS OWN TRUNK, so the animal stands close to the ground with its back low and level and only a shallow gap beneath the belly. A large rodent with a blunt rounded muzzle, upright ears shorter and more rounded than a hare's, slender hoof-like feet, a grey-brown coat, a white patch across the rump edged above by a dark band, and almost no visible tail.
mantis: A scientific field-guide illustration of a praying mantis perched on a leaf, seen in STRICT SIDE PROFILE. IT HAS SIX LEGS IN TOTAL AND NO MORE: at the front, TWO raptorial forelegs, thickened and spined, folded up beneath the head; behind them, FOUR slender walking legs, TWO on each side, spaced evenly along the middle and rear of the thorax and carrying the body. Six legs altogether, all attached to the thorax, and the long abdomen behind them is completely bare of limbs. An elongated green body, a small triangular head with large eyes turned toward the viewer, and long thread-like antennae.
loris: A scientific field-guide illustration of a slow loris clinging to a VERTICAL branch, seen in STRICT SIDE PROFILE, its body upright against the wood. EACH OF ITS FOUR HANDS IS A SIMPLE ROUNDED GRASPING PAD WRAPPED RIGHT AROUND THE BRANCH: the thumb reaches far out to one side, almost opposite the other digits, and closes against them so the branch is held in a firm pincer between thumb and fingers. The digits are SHORT, THICK AND EVEN, each ending in a small flat nail, and they curl closely over the wood with the palm pressed flat to it. All four hands grip in the same way. A small round-bodied primate with dense grey-brown fur, a dark stripe down the spine, huge round forward-facing eyes ringed with dark patches, tiny ears and no tail.
snubnosed: A scientific field-guide illustration of a golden snub-nosed monkey on all fours on a branch, both hands and both feet flat on the wood, seen in STRICT SIDE PROFILE. ITS BUILD IS SLIGHT AND MONKEY-LIKE: a SLENDER SHALLOW TORSO no deeper from back to belly than the length of its own head, narrow shoulders no wider than its hips, thin limbs of even thickness, and a LONG TAIL AS LONG AS ITS BODY hanging down behind. Its back is nearly level, its chest is narrow and flat, and it is small and light. Long golden-orange fur over the shoulders and flanks, a flat pale blue face with a small upturned nose, and pale tufts at the corners of the mouth.
wallaby: A scientific field-guide illustration of a wallaby sitting back on its hind feet and tail in STRICT SIDE PROFILE. ITS BUILD IS SMALL AND ROUNDED: a compact marsupial with a PLUMP ROUNDED BACK CURVING IN ONE SMOOTH ARC from the neck to the base of the tail, a deep rounded chest and belly, SHORT hind legs bent close beneath it, and a short blunt face on a small rounded head. The whole animal is a soft rounded shape rather than a tall angular one, standing no higher than the length of its own body. Grey-brown fur, small forepaws held at its chest, short rounded ears and a thick tapering tail resting along the ground.
frilledshark: A scientific field-guide illustration of a frilled shark in STRICT SIDE PROFILE, its long slender brown eel-like body curving in loose waves, head to the left. THE HEAD IS BROAD AND FLATTENED FROM ABOVE, wider than it is deep, ending in a BLUNT SQUARE FRONT. THE MOUTH IS AT THE VERY FRONT TIP OF THE FACE: the jaw line runs straight across the leading edge of the head so the mouth opens forward, and the snout does not project beyond it — the profile of the head ends where the mouth begins, in one flat vertical face. The wide mouth is lined with small three-pronged needle teeth. Small round eyes set far forward on the sides of the head. Immediately behind the head, SIX PAIRS OF RUFFLED FRILLY GILL SLITS with loose fringed edges, the first pair meeting beneath the throat. A long tapering tail.
leatherback: A scientific field-guide illustration of a leatherback turtle swimming, seen in three-quarter view from above and the side. ITS SHELL IS A SMOOTH TEARDROP: broad and rounded across the shoulders, narrowing steadily backward to a BLUNT POINT over the tail, and low and streamlined in cross-section rather than domed. THE SHELL SURFACE IS UNBROKEN RUBBERY LEATHERY SKIN, dark grey-black flecked with pale spots, with NO plates, NO scutes and NO tiled pattern anywhere; running along its length are SEVEN NARROW RAISED RIDGES running the length of the shell, evenly spaced from front to back. Its front flippers are ENORMOUS, each one as long as the shell itself, and it has no claws. A small head with a deeply notched upper jaw.
oarfish: A scientific field-guide illustration of an extremely long silver oarfish in STRICT FLAT SIDE PROFILE, hanging vertically in deep water with its whole length turned broadside to the viewer. THE PROPORTIONS ARE THE POINT: its body is a very narrow flattened band, AT LEAST THIRTY TIMES LONGER THAN IT IS DEEP, running the full height of the picture from top to bottom. ALONG THAT LENGTH IT UNDULATES IN FOUR OR FIVE DEEP SMOOTH S-CURVES, swinging well out to one side and back again so the body waves loosely from end to end, never straight. It tapers away smoothly to a fine thread at its lower end and simply stops. A crimson fin of short rays runs the entire length of its back. A tall crest of long red plumes rises from the top of its small blunt head, and two long red oar-shaped fins trail from just behind it. Silvery skin flecked with dark spots, one large dark eye.
sunfishmola: A scientific field-guide illustration of an ocean sunfish seen from the side, mouth at the front on the left. ITS BODY IS VERY NEARLY A CIRCLE: a great round flattened disc almost exactly AS TALL AS IT IS LONG, its outline curving smoothly and evenly all the way round from the top of the back, down past the blunt face, along the belly and back up. The whole animal ENDS ABRUPTLY a short way behind the eye in a blunt vertical edge finished with a small wavy scalloped frill lying flat against it, and past that frill there is nothing. From the top one enormous pointed fin rises straight UP and from the bottom an identical one points straight DOWN, each about as long as the body is deep. Its expression is comically vacant: one small round eye set high and far forward, and a TINY ROUND PUCKERED MOUTH permanently open in a small O. Rough mottled silver-grey hide, small pectoral fins.
pilotwhale: A scientific field-guide illustration of a long-finned pilot whale in STRICT SIDE PROFILE, swimming level. ITS PROPORTIONS ARE THE POINT: the body is LONG AND SLENDER, running from the front of the head to the tail flukes at ABOUT SIX TIMES ITS OWN GREATEST DEPTH, tapering smoothly along a slim tail stock. ITS HEAD IS A LARGE SMOOTH BULB: the forehead swells forward and upward into a THICK ROUNDED MELON that overhangs the mouthline and is evenly rounded across the front, with no beak and no crease. Dark black-grey skin, a pale grey saddle behind the dorsal fin, and very long narrow pointed flippers set low on the chest. A low broad-based dorsal fin curving backward, set forward of the middle of the back.
rissos: A scientific field-guide illustration of a Risso's dolphin in STRICT SIDE PROFILE, swimming level. ITS PROPORTIONS ARE THE POINT: the body is LONG, about SIX TIMES ITS OWN GREATEST DEPTH from the front of the head to the tail flukes, deepest at the shoulder and tapering steadily to a slim tail stock. ITS HEAD IS A LARGE SMOOTH BULB, blunt and evenly rounded across the whole front with no beak and no snout whatsoever, the forehead rising in one broad curve from the mouthline, and split by a distinct vertical crease down the centre of the melon. Its pale grey body is criss-crossed all over with dense white scratches and scars, and it carries a tall curved dorsal fin.
spinnerdolphin: A scientific field-guide illustration of a spinner dolphin in STRICT SIDE PROFILE, swimming level. ITS PROPORTIONS ARE THE POINT: the body is LONG AND VERY SLIM, running from the tip of the beak to the tail flukes at ABOUT SEVEN TIMES ITS OWN GREATEST DEPTH, a slender shallow torpedo that tapers evenly to a narrow tail stock, noticeably thin for its length. A long thin beak clearly separated from the forehead by a crease, a tall nearly triangular dorsal fin at the middle of the back, and slender pointed flippers. Dark grey back, pale grey flanks and a white belly in three distinct bands.
